withholding.name: Mississippi Department of Revenue, Income Tax Bureau

efile.text: Electronic reporting through Taxpayer Access Point (TAP) is mandatory for employers submitting 10 or more W-2s or 1099s.

deposits.interpretation: Mississippi's Department of Revenue determines whether an employer files MONTHLY or QUARTERLY and tells it so; the guide gives no dollar thresholds, so the frequency is an INPUT and is never derived (a look-back amount draws an error, not a guess). Monthly: return and remittance by the 15th of the following month. Quarterly: return and remittance by the 15th of the month after the quarter (April 15, July 15, October 15, January 15). A return is filed for every period even with no tax due. A due date on a weekend or state holiday moves to the next working day.

lookback.description: None: the Department assigns the frequency

returns.name: Mississippi monthly or quarterly withholding return (Form 89-105 coupon for paper filers)
contents: Filed for every period even if no tax is due, on the frequency the Department assigns.
Paper filers (fewer than 10 W-2s or 1099s) use the preaddressed Form 89-105 coupons.

returns.name: Annual Information Return, Form 89-140, with W-2s
contents: W-2s and the Annual Information Return are due to the State by January 31; 1099s with it by February 28.
W-2s are submitted in SSA EFW2 format including the RS record; 1099s in IRS Publication 1220 format.
Penalty for not filing electronically when required: $25 first instance, $500 each additional instance.

notModelled: Mississippi unemployment insurance (Mississippi Department of Employment Security): no document read.
The thresholds the Department uses to assign monthly or quarterly: not in the guide.
Mississippi's state-holiday list (weekends only are skipped, with a warning).
The January 31 W-2 date is used for the annual return; the February 28 date for 1099s is recorded in the contents only.

channels.function: withholding returns and payments, W-2/1099 filing, bulk filing through FSET
channels.description: Mississippi Taxpayer Access Point (TAP); the Fed/State Employment Taxes (FSET) program lets payroll software transmit returns and payments in bulk
enrollment: Register for a Mississippi withholding account (steps not read).
Employers with 10 or more W-2s or 1099s must file through TAP; payroll software that participates in FSET can transmit returns and payment information to the Department in bulk without TAP.
channels.specs: W-2: SSA EFW2 with the RS state record; other information returns: IRS Publication 1220. FSET layouts were not read.
